summary: Ween is the duo of Aaron Freeman and Mickey Melchiondo, who hop between genres with deadpan humor and real musical skill. They grew from lo-fi home tapes into a cult touring band with a devoted following.
know: Freeman and Melchiondo met as teenagers and performed as Gene Ween and Dean Ween.
12 Golden Country Greats was cut in Nashville with veteran session players.
The Mollusk is a sea-themed record that mixes prog, folk and psychedelic pop.

influencedBy.why: Zappa's mix of genre parody and serious chops is the closest model for Ween's approach.
Melchiondo has often named Prince as a favorite, and his falsetto funk shows up across Ween records.
The Butthole Surfers' warped, tape-manipulated rock shaped Ween's early lo-fi sound.
Ween's pop songwriting and studio play draw on late-1960s Beatles records.
Songs like Voodoo Lady borrow Funkadelic's loose, heavy funk-rock feel.

influenced.why: Phish took Roses Are Free into its live repertoire, linking the two bands' audiences.

cousins.why: Genre-hopping musical comedy played with real skill.
Deadpan pastiche songs that work as music, not just jokes.

summary: Phish is a Vermont quartet built on long improvisation, complex composed pieces and constantly changing setlists. They became the leading American jam band of the 1990s and beyond.
know: The band formed at the University of Vermont with Trey Anastasio, Mike Gordon, Jon Fishman and Page McConnell.
Their Halloween shows have covered entire albums by other artists, including the Beatles' White Album and Talking Heads' Remain in Light.
They rarely repeat a setlist, which drives a large culture of fans taping and trading shows.

influencedBy.why: The Dead's model of open improvisation and touring culture is the blueprint Phish built on.
Anastasio's tightly composed, tricky instrumental sections echo Zappa's writing.
Phish covered Remain in Light in full and absorbed its interlocking grooves.
Their 1994 White Album set reflects how deeply the band knows Beatles songcraft.
The band's odd meters and prog structures follow King Crimson's lead.
Anastasio's early long-form suites draw on 1970s Genesis.

cousins.why: Group improvisation where every player steers the music.
Long, exploratory jams rooted in a different tradition.

summary: Muse is a trio led by Matt Bellamy that pairs heavy riffs with classical piano and huge, theatrical arrangements. They grew into one of the biggest stadium rock bands of the 2000s.
know: The lineup of Matt Bellamy, Chris Wolstenholme and Dominic Howard has not changed since the band's start.
Bellamy's piano parts borrow openly from Romantic classical composers such as Rachmaninoff.
They won the Grammy for Best Rock Album for The Resistance and again for Drones.

influencedBy.why: Muse's early records were often compared to The Bends for their falsetto and guitar drama.
Layered harmonies and operatic rock moments on later albums follow Queen's example.
Bellamy has cited Buckley's soaring voice as a key model for his singing.
The band started out playing grunge-inspired rock in Devon.
Wolstenholme's heavy, riff-driven bass lines share Rage's attack.
Big walls of guitar with tender quiet sections mirror the Pumpkins' dynamics.

cousins.why: Virtuosic, maximal rock with prog ambition.
Classical-leaning prog played with metal force.
Theatrical, genre-blending heavy music aimed at big rooms.

summary: Jethro Tull is Ian Anderson's band, known for lead flute, English folk melodies and long progressive pieces. They moved from the British blues boom into concept albums and folk rock.
know: Ian Anderson's flute playing, often while standing on one leg, became the band's signature.
Thick as a Brick is a single album-length song presented as a parody of concept albums.
Crest of a Knave won the first Grammy for Best Hard Rock/Metal Performance in 1989.

influencedBy.why: Tull began in the same British blues club circuit that Mayall's band led.
Their first album This Was is built largely on Chicago blues forms.
The English folk rock that Fairport pioneered fed Tull's later folk turn, and Fairport's Dave Pegg later joined Tull.

influenced.why: Steve Harris has named Tull as a major influence, and Maiden covered Cross-Eyed Mary.
Mikael Akerfeldt has cited Tull's folk-prog writing as an influence on Opeth's quieter side.

cousins.why: Traditional English melody fused with electric rock.
Flute and whistle as lead voices in a folk setting.

summary: Emerson, Lake & Palmer was a keyboard-led trio that adapted classical works and wrote long suites for rock band. Keith Emerson's organ and Moog playing defined much of 1970s progressive rock.
know: The members came from the Nice, King Crimson and Atomic Rooster.
Lucky Man ends with one of the first well-known Moog synthesizer solos on a rock hit.
They recorded rock versions of Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition and Copland's Fanfare for the Common Man.

influencedBy.why: Greg Lake sang and played bass on King Crimson's debut before forming ELP.
Emerson's earlier band the Nice built its Rondo on Brubeck's Blue Rondo a la Turk.
Procol Harum showed that classical themes and organ could carry a rock hit.
The Moody Blues' orchestral rock pointed toward ELP's symphonic scale.

influenced.why: Keyboardist Jordan Rudess has named Emerson as a key influence on his playing.
Rush's long multi-part suites of the mid-1970s followed the path ELP laid out.
Kansas's keyboard-heavy American prog draws on ELP's style.

cousins.why: Classical repertoire reimagined on the Moog synthesizer.
Grand, keyboard-built music with classical scale.

summary: Camel is a melodic English progressive rock band led by guitarist and flautist Andrew Latimer. Their mostly instrumental 1970s albums favor lyrical guitar lines and atmosphere over showy complexity.
know: Andrew Latimer has been the one constant member across the band's history.
The Snow Goose is an instrumental album based on Paul Gallico's novella, later performed with the London Symphony Orchestra at the Royal Albert Hall.
Bassist and singer Richard Sinclair of Caravan joined in 1977.

influencedBy.why: Latimer's slow, sustained guitar tone sits close to David Gilmour's.
Camel shares the gentle, jazz-tinged Canterbury feel, and later hired Caravan's Richard Sinclair.
Long symphonic arrangements on Mirage follow the path Yes opened.
Mellotron textures and extended instrumentals trace back to King Crimson's debut.

Marillion's melodic neo-prog guitar leads echo Latimer's style.
Steven Wilson's atmospheric instrumental passages draw on Camel-style melodic prog.

cousins.why: Mostly instrumental music built on mood and slow build.
Wide, melodic soundscapes that tell a story without many words.

summary: Gentle Giant was a progressive rock band of multi-instrumentalists known for intricate counterpoint, medieval-style vocal harmony and sudden shifts in meter. They are a musicians' favorite for their compositional density.
know: The Shulman brothers Derek, Ray and Phil had earlier been in the pop group Simon Dupree and the Big Sound.
Members switched among dozens of instruments on stage, including violin, cello, recorder and vibraphone.

influencedBy.why: King Crimson's debut showed the band how far rock structure could stretch.
Zappa's tightly written, rhythmically tricky rock is a close cousin to their writing.
The Shulmans came out of the 1960s pop world shaped by the Beatles' studio experiments.

influenced.why: Mike Portnoy and other Dream Theater members have praised Gentle Giant's complex writing.

cousins.why: Dense, intricate vocal harmony and multi-instrumental arranging.
Interlocking parts that click together like clockwork.

summary: Van der Graaf Generator is Peter Hammill's band, a darker and more abrasive strand of progressive rock built on organ, saxophone and intense vocals. They were a key influence on later punk and post-punk singers.
know: The band formed at the University of Manchester around singer and writer Peter Hammill.
Robert Fripp played guitar as a guest on H to He, Who Am the Only One and Pawn Hearts.
David Jackson often played two saxophones at once through effects pedals.

Mikael Akerfeldt has named Van der Graaf as a key influence on Opeth's darker prog.

Gothic theater and abrasive textures.

summary: Soft Machine was the founding band of the Canterbury scene, moving from psychedelic pop to long, jazz-based instrumental pieces. They were among the first British rock bands to fully embrace jazz improvisation.
know: Early members included Robert Wyatt, Kevin Ayers, Mike Ratledge and Daevid Allen.
They supported the Jimi Hendrix Experience on its 1968 North American tour.

influencedBy.why: Their turn to electric jazz around Third followed the same direction as Miles Davis.
Long modal improvisation in their instrumentals draws on Coltrane.
Free jazz shaped Elton Dean's and Ratledge's more open playing.
Their first psychedelic pop songs grew out of the Beatles era.

Camel absorbed the jazz-leaning Canterbury sound Soft Machine started.

cousins.why: Electric jazz built on long group pieces.
Instrumental rock that borrows jazz structure.

summary: Caravan is a Canterbury band known for gentle, whimsical songs that open into long jazz-flavored instrumental passages. In the Land of Grey and Pink is a defining record of the scene.

cousins.why: Soft English voice with quiet, pastoral songwriting.
Gentle, whimsical keyboard-led melody.

summary: Procol Harum combined Gary Brooker's soulful piano and voice, Hammond organ and Keith Reid's lyrics into a stately, classical-tinged rock. Their debut single became one of the most played songs of the 1960s.

summary: The Moody Blues began as an R&B beat group and reinvented themselves as pioneers of orchestral, Mellotron-based rock. Days of Future Passed helped launch the idea of the rock concept album.

Rick Davies's blues and R&B keyboard style traces back to Ray Charles.
Keyboard-led English art rock with strong melodies follows Procol Harum.

Keyboard-led 1970s pop rock with art-rock touches.

summary: Kansas brought British-style progressive rock to the American heartland, adding violin and boogie-rock power. Carry On Wayward Son and Dust in the Wind made them a fixture of classic rock radio.

summary: Marillion led the 1980s revival of progressive rock, first with the theatrical Fish and then with Steve Hogarth. They later pioneered fan-funded recording.
